$comment: Non-secret deployment configuration for StudioCRM. Committed on purpose: none of it is
sensitive. Every credential — the GitHub token, DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, the FTP password,
the deploy hook URL — stays OUT of this file and out of git. See docs/DEPLOYMENT.md.
The host BUILDS in a Linux container from a git clone and RUNS on Windows under IIS, which
starts Node through httpPlatformHandler from web.config. Established from the host's own
deploy log and from the deployed files, not assumed. So FTP is not how the app is deployed -
but it IS how the host's logs are read and how web.config is repaired after every deploy,
because the host rewrites it into a version that starts nothing.
Values marked TODO must be read from the SmarterASP.NET / Site4Now control panel. Do not
guess them: a wrong appUrl makes the health check pass against nothing.

panel.$deployTarget: What the panel's Node app page shows as the deploy target for this site.

git.$branch: The branch the panel clones, and it must match what the panel is set to. main is the deployed branch on purpose: the panel already points at it, so there is one fewer place for 'live' and 'main' to drift apart. Feature branches merge into main before a deploy, never instead of it.
git.$auth: The repository is PUBLIC (verified against the GitHub API), so the panel needs no Deployment Key and the clone works unauthenticated - which is how the currently live build got there. If it is ever made private, the panel needs a GitHub Personal Access Token with read access; that token is pasted into the panel by hand and is never stored here, in git, or in any script.

build.$command: Explicit, because the panel's npm default cannot resolve this repo's workspace:* dependencies, and because --prod=false keeps the devDependencies the web build needs even if NODE_ENV=production is set during install.
build.$start: Runs apps/api/dist/server.js — the single bundle that serves /api and the React build.

$appUrl: The public https:// URL of the site: the client-review link and the base every verification runs against. A valid certificate is served on it and the host already serves an app there, so this is confirmed, not guessed.

logs.$why: FTPS over port 21 (the server's own FEAT advertises AUTH TLS), landing directly on the site root. Two jobs: reading the host's own logs (node_app_automate_deploy_<id>.log for the build, logs\node.log for the running process), and re-uploading web.config after each deploy. The application itself is never deployed this way - the host's git pipeline does that. The password is never stored here; it comes from $env:STUDIOCRM_FTP_PASSWORD, deploy/.env.deploy (gitignored), or a prompt.
